query: My 2020 crossover shows a tire pressure warning light and the tires are worn out. Is it smart to replace the sensors when I buy tires?
expected_behavior: Checks pressure first, then explains a sensor fault versus low air
Notes sensor batteries are sealed and last roughly 5-10 years, and that replacing at tire-change time saves a second labor charge
Mentions relearn/programming and marks sensor type and cost [verify]

query: Compare tires for my 2014 sedan that a teenager drives only short trips. Give me a link to buy each option and tell me if labor is included.
expected_behavior: Treats age/sidewall condition and budget tier as more relevant than treadwear for a low-mileage car
Gives one purchase link per shortlisted tire or says a retailer page could not be loaded and marks the price [verify]
Shows labor as its own line item and states whether totals include it

query: Is Joe's Tire Shop a good place to get these installed? Write it up as a PDF-ready report.
expected_behavior: Bases the shop assessment only on evidence found (reviews, certifications, written quote) and does not invent prices or reputation
Says what could not be verified
Report includes fitment, shortlist table, itemized installed cost with labor, TPMS notes, and links with dated sources
